title: Hagelloch 1861: the time to the rash nearly fixed, 12 to 13 days, the prodrome from the record within it

source.citation: Pfeilsticker A. Beiträge zur Pathologie der Masern mit besonderer Berücksichtigung der statistischen Verhältnisse. Tübingen: Eberhard-Karls-Universität; 1863.
source.read: OCR text of the incubation chapter, 2026-11-18

evidence.quote: dass die Zeit von der Ansteckung bis zur Eruption … constant 14 Tage sei (that the time from infection to the rash is a constant 14 days)
evidence.working: Infection to the rash 12 to 13 days, less a prodrome of 2: 10 to 11 days. 12 to 13 is the record's latent period (median 8.5, experiment 199) and prodrome (mean 4) together, held nearly fixed as the rule of 1863 holds it fixed.
evidence.note: Pfeilsticker's 14 days is from infection; the model's day of infection is the day of transmission, and the record's intervals give 12 to 13. A sensitivity runs others.

source.citation: Measles in Hagelloch, Germany, 1861: 188 children, from Pfeilsticker (1863) as reanalysed by Oesterle (1992), in the outbreaks R package 1.9.0 (measles_hagelloch_1861); examples/hagelloch-1861/cases.json in this repository.

evidence.working: Each prodrome length a branch of its own: 2 days.
